radiology_report:
RAD-2025-0205 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate | 05 Feb 2025

Clinical Indication:
Re-evaluation of established prostate malignancy. Current PSA 8.6 ng/mL. Prior imaging displayed PI-RADS 5.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume measures 42.65 mL. A discrete focus sits in the right posterior peripheral zone at the base-to-mid junction, spanning 18 x 15 x 12 mm. The area shows intense DWI restriction with low ADC values, T2 hypointensity, and early focal enhancement on dynamic contrast sequences. Seminal vesicles remain clear. No extraprostatic extension or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is detected.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right posterior peripheral zone.
PSA density: 0.202 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8539465.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. van den Berg (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial workup triggered by an incidental PSA reading of 5.5 ng/mL back in April 2023. Follow-up surveillance showed a steady upward trend, leading to a transrectal ultrasound-guided needle sampling that confirmed adenocarcinoma. With the diagnosis secured and PSA levels continuing to climb, the clinical focus shifted toward specialist review.
